name: Google Cybersecurity Professional Certificate

fee.note: Paid as a monthly Coursera subscription: US$49 a month in the U.S. and Canada after a 7-day free trial, so the total depends on how long you take. Coursera says most learners finish in under six months for less than US$300, and the price may be lower in other countries. Coursera financial aid can lower the cost but not cover it in full.

exam.format: No final proctored exam. The certificate is earned by passing the graded assignments (mostly quizzes) in each course of the online program, alongside hands-on labs and portfolio activities. Self-paced; Coursera estimates 6 months at about 7 hours a week (170 hours of instruction).

scope: Entry-level security analyst skills: security frameworks and controls, risk management, networks and network security, Linux and SQL, assets, threats and vulnerabilities, detection and incident response with SIEM tools (Chronicle, Splunk) and IDS (Suricata), Python automation, and job search preparation, with AI used for security tasks.
requirements: No prior experience or degree required.
ai_policy: Check the current assessment rules. AI-assisted study does not imply permission during the exam.
caveats: Coursera's program page lists nine courses (the newest, 'Accelerate Your Job Search with AI', is about the job search) while its description and FAQ still say eight.

Spanish: Google's courses taught in Spanish ('Fundamentos de la ciberseguridad' and the rest) are online and listed as part of the 'Ciberseguridad de Google' certificate, but that program's own Coursera address now opens the English program, which offers Spanish only as an automatic translation of the instructional content. Check the language when you enroll.
This is a course certificate, not a proctored certification. Google says it helps prepare for CompTIA Security+ and that graduates get the Security+ exam and training at a discounted price.

On completion you can claim a Credly badge carrying an ACE recommendation of up to 9 college credits (7 ECTS); each institution decides whether to accept it. Google's employer consortiums (150+ employers in the U.S.) currently run in the U.S., Canada, India, Singapore and Indonesia.
